title: Rabbi Levi bar Nezira
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Yerushalmi Berakhot, chapter 2, at the end of halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.1.17), he said: “Whenever someone recites a teaching in the name of the one who said it, the latter’s lips stir with him in the grave.”
In [Yevamot 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.97a), the saying is cited in the name of Shimon Nezira.[^1]

notes.text: In Yevamot 97a, Rabbi Yochanan transmits the saying in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name; Rabbi Yitzchak ben Zeira—or, alternatively, Shimon Nezira—supplies its scriptural basis.
